newsitem.title: INDIA: India train bomb kills 22, 45 people injured - UNI.
newsitem.headline: India train bomb kills 22, 45 people injured - UNI.

text.p: Twenty-two people were killed and 45 injured when a powerful bomb exploded on a train in the northern Indian state of Punjab on Tuesday, the United News of India (UNI) said.
UNI said the explosion occurred at a railway station in Lehrakhanna town in the northern state of Punjab.
The Press Trust of India said the blast occurred at about 2 p.m. (0830 GMT).
Punjab, one of India's most prosperous states, was rocked by a bloody Sikh separatist insurgency in the 1980s. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.

In August 1995, the state's chief minister Beant Singh was killed when a bomb planted in his chauffeur-driven car exploded. At least seven people were killed in March in a bomb blast in Punjab near a busy railway station.
